objects.name: a folded stack of evening papers

people.name: Antonio Marchetti
people.role: a photographer for the rotogravure section

secret.description: Antonio Marchetti is alone with Maureen Quill in the Service Stairs from 10:00 PM to 10:30 PM, and kills Maureen Quill at 10:30 PM.
Willa Prentiss hands a parcel of stolen goods to a man at the Kitchen at 10:30 PM.
Delia Mulcahy slips out to the Street from 6:30 PM to 7:00 PM to settle with a bookmaker.

people.name: Marion Winslow
people.role: a wine steward out of work since the Act

secret.description: Marion Winslow is not the person the register says. Nothing is hidden about the evening; the lie is in the paperwork.

people.name: Lorraine Ashby
people.role: a stringer for the evening papers

secret.description: Lorraine Ashby goes through the papers in the Victim's Suite from 8:00 PM while the victim is downstairs.

people.name: Beatrice Ellery
people.relationshipToVictim: a childhood friend of the victim from the same block

secret.description: Beatrice Ellery drinks alone in the Bar from 10:00 PM to 10:30 PM and will claim to have been anywhere else.

method.name: strangling with a cord
method.bodyEvidence: A ligature furrow across the throat. Three fibres of hemp in the skin.

Maureen Quill was found on the Service Stairs. The coroner puts death between 10:00 PM and 10:30 PM. A ligature furrow across the throat. Three fibres of hemp in the skin.
A length of sash cord is missing from the Kitchen. A cut end of the same hemp is still tied to the fitting it was taken from.
Rain began at 9:30 PM and did not let up. Anyone out on the street after that came back in wet.
Delia Mulcahy says Lorraine Ashby came in off the street at 10:00 PM with a soaked coat, so Lorraine Ashby was outside at 9:30 PM.
Marion Winslow's papers do not hold up. The registration card gives an address in Buffalo. There is no such street in Buffalo.
Found in the Victim's Suite: A subpoena naming Maureen Quill as a witness before the grand jury, with Antonio Marchetti's name written in the margin.
Harriet Havemeyer says Maureen Quill said to Antonio Marchetti that a man who testifies sleeps better.
Found in the Front Desk: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Willa Prentiss, endorsed to Maureen Quill, three months past due.
Delia Mulcahy says Maureen Quill told Willa Prentiss that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Found in the Victim's Suite: Three letters in Maureen Quill's hand to a woman Lorraine Ashby is engaged to, kept in the drawer, the last one opened.
Martin Feeney says Lorraine Ashby told Maureen Quill to keep away, loud enough to turn heads.
